hook.text: One person shares a rumor. Ten share it from them. Hundreds share from those ten. In hours, millions 'know' a lie.

buildup.text: Information cascades happen when people adopt a belief because others have, not because of personal evidence.

discovery.text: Each share adds perceived credibility. If many people believe it, your brain assumes there must be a reason.

twist.text: The original claim may have been baseless. But by the time it reaches you, it looks well-established.

climax.text: Cascades are fragile — built on imitation, not evidence. But they move faster than corrections ever can.

punchline.text: A million shares don't make it true. They just make it popular.

quiz.question: What drives an information cascade?
options: People adopt beliefs because others have, not from personal evidence
